payload.title: Tidy public wording: registry mirror note and conduct contact
payload.body:
Two small in-tree items from the 2026-11-10 open-source safety audit. (1) .github/workflows/tasks-claim-check.yml line 35 names a specific registry-mirror product in a comment; AGENTS.md, docs/release-and-ci.md, .github/workflows/tasks-snapshot.yml and packages/cli/src/commands/fleet.ts say 'registry mirror'. Use the generic wording everywhere. (2) CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md line 59 sends private conduct reports to an address on the tasks.md domain, which a third party owns (see set-up-github-pages-custom-domain). Replace it with a contact the owner controls, for example GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the owner's public address. The owner picks the contact.
- **Hypothesis**: a conduct contact the owner controls means a private report reaches the maintainer; contact addresses on domains the project does not own drop from 1 to 0.
- **Measurement**: grep -c '@tasks.md' CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
- **Success**: the command prints 0 and npm run lint passes.
- **Pivot**: if the owner wants no email contact, point the section at GitHub's report-abuse flow and close the task.
- **Anchor**: Contributor Covenant 2.1, Enforcement section; GitHub docs 'Adding a code of conduct to your project'.
